cards.a: REST is an HTTP-based API style where resources are URL-addressable and actions are HTTP verbs (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) carrying JSON or XML data. Network controllers like DNA Center, SD-WAN vManage, and routers via RESTCONF expose REST APIs, making the network scriptable.

cards.q: What are the core principles of REST?
cards.a: Resources are URL-addressable, actions use HTTP verbs, requests are stateless (each request is independent), and data is carried as JSON/XML.

cards.q: What is the meaning of each HTTP verb in REST?
cards.a: GET = read, POST = create, PUT = replace, PATCH = modify, and DELETE = remove.

cards.q: What do the common HTTP status codes 200, 201, 401, 404, and 500 mean?
cards.a: 200 = OK, 201 = created, 401 = unauthorized, 404 = not found, and 500 = server error. In general 2xx = success, 4xx = client error, 5xx = server error.

cards.q: How is a REST API request structured?
cards.a: It has a base URL (e.g., https://controller), a path (e.g., /dna/intent/api/...), token/header-based authentication, and a JSON payload body. Token-based auth such as OAuth/bearer is standard.

cards.q: What do the cURL flags -X, -H, -d, and -k do?
cards.a: -X sets the HTTP verb, -H adds headers, -d sends a JSON body, and -k skips TLS certificate verification. Example: curl -X GET -H "X-Auth-Token: $TOKEN" -k against the DNA Center network-device endpoint.

cards.q: Why is REST the automation gateway for SDN and controllers?
cards.a: It enables scripting/automation, provides the same consistent API for read and write (full device lifecycle), and integrates with tools like Ansible and Python.

cards.q: How do you troubleshoot REST API failures?
cards.a: 401 = bad token (check auth), 404 = wrong path (check URL), 500 = server problem (check logs), timeout = reachability to the base URL, and 400 = bad JSON body.

cards.q: Which verb replaces an entire REST resource for a network change?
cards.a: PUT replaces the resource; PATCH performs a partial update, POST creates, and DELETE removes. GET only reads.

cards.q: What is the state model of REST requests?
cards.a: REST requests are stateless: every request is independent and carries what it needs, so the server keeps no session state between calls.
